https://telex.hu/belfold/2026/09/04/a-ko.text: Menü Kereső Lannert Judit: Újraindul az Erasmus a magyar egyetemeken Belföld Aradi Hanga Zsófia Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom Minden magyar egyetemre visszatér az Erasmus program – jelentette be Lannert Judit gyermek- és oktatásügyi miniszter a Facebookon . Lannert azt írta, a magyar kormány augusztus végéig minden szükséges lépést megtett azért, hogy az Erasmus program újra elérhető legyen a magyar egyetemisták számára, így már a korlátozással érintett 21 egyetem is rendelkezik érvényes Erasmus mobilitási pályázattal a 2026/2027-es tanévre. „Az Erasmus így visszatérhet ezekre a magyar egyetemekre is, és ismét megnyílnak a nemzetközi mobilitás lehetőségei a hallgatók előtt” – írta. Az Európai Unió által zárolt pénzek hazahozatalának egyik feltétele volt a felsőoktatási rendszer átalakítása, aminek augusztusig kellett megtörténnie. Erre azért volt szükség, hogy az egyetemi és innovációs források újra elérhetővé váljanak, vagyis hogy a hallgatók visszatérhessenek az Erasmus-programba, a kutatók és a kutatásfejlesztésben résztvevők pedig a Horizon-programokhoz. Görög Márta igazságügyi miniszter korábban arról beszélt , az átalakítás nemcsak az egyetemeket fenntartó kekvákat érinti ( erről itt írtunk bővebben ), a jövőben minden egyetemen egységes szabályok garantálják majd a hallgatói képviseletet is, és az egyetemi közösség részvételét a döntéshozatalban. A szenátus tagjait az egyetemi közösség választja majd meg, a rektort pedig a szenátus, és ahol ezek a szabályok jelenleg nem érvényesülnek, új szenátust kell választani az igazságügyi miniszter szerint. Az EU tagállamai 2022-ben szinte egyhangú szavazással tiltottak el minden közérdekű vagyonkezelő alapítványt (kekvát) az uniós forrásoktól, a határozatot azok átláthatósági és összeférhetetlenségi problémáival indokolva. Idén májusban az Európai Bizottság elnöke és az új magyar miniszterelnök közös sajtótájékoztatón jelentette be, hogy Magyarország rövid határidőn belül kivezeti a közérdekű vagyonkezelő alapítványokat, és olyan rendszert fog bevezetni, amely biztosítja az integritási szabályok érvényesülését. Bár a Tisza-kormány az utolsó pillanatra minden szükséges dokumentumot beszerzett az uniós helyreállítási alap feltételeinek teljesítéséhez, az Erasmus esetében jellemzően nyár közepén szokták megkötni azokat a kétéves szerződéseket, amelyek 2024 szeptemberére mind kipörögtek , és nem lehetett újra aláírni a tiltás miatt. Így nehezen elképzelhető, hogy az évkezdésre minden kekvás egyetem visszatérhessen a programba. Kedvenceink Partnereinktől Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Photograph: Spencer Platt/Getty Images September 11 2001 Remembrance ceremonies to be held across the US to honor victims of 9/11 Memorials and remembrances will mark the 25 years since the attacks that killed nearly 3,000 on 11 September 2001 US marks 25 years since 9/11 – latest updates Anna Betts in New York Fri 11 Sep 2026 04.00 EDT Last modified on Fri 11 Sep 2026 06.18 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google The United States is marking the 25th anniversary of the 11 September 2001 terrorist attacks on Friday, with memorials and remembrance ceremonies taking place across the country to honor the nearly 3,000 people killed in the attacks. In New York City , the national September 11 memorial and museum will hold its annual commemoration ceremony, with the families of victims gathering at the 9/11 Memorial Plaza and reading aloud the names of those killed in the 9/11 attacks and in the 1993 World Trade Center bombing. The 25th commemoration ceremony will begin at 8:30am local time. Seven moments of silence will be observed throughout the ceremony, marking the times when each of the towers was struck and fell, as well as the times of the attack on the Pentagon in Arlington county, Virginia, and the crash of Flight 93 in Pennsylvania, “and to honor those who lost their lives to 9/11-related illness and injury in the years since”, according to the museum. Americans on how 9/11 changed their lives: ‘It completely unraveled the US’ Read more Current and former New York City leaders and other political figures are also expected to attend the ceremony, including the city’s mayor , Zohran Mamdani. The New York Times reported this month that former president Joe Biden and former first lady Jill Biden, as well as former presidents Barack Obama, George W Bush and Bill Clinton, and former secretary of state Hillary Clinton, are also expected to attend. Donald Trump is expected to commemorate the anniversary at the Pentagon , where American Airlines Flight 77 crashed after being hijacked . JD Vance is expected to attend the New York ceremony. On Wednesday night in New York City, a drone show featuring 2,977 lights , one for each person killed in the attacks, illuminated the skies over New York Harbor, before forming the outline of the twin towers. Friday’s memorial ceremonies come just days after the Mamdani administration released more than 170,000 documents related to the health concerns, air quality and city’s response to the attacks, including records suggesting that New Yorkers were misled about the safety of the air quality after the attacks. Also on Friday morning, New York City firefighters are scheduled to hold a ceremony at the FDNY firefighters memorial on Manhattan’s Upper West Side to honor the 343 members of the department who lost their lives on September 11. In Virginia, the national 9/11 Pentagon memorial will be closed to the public from 3am through noon on Friday for the Pentagon’s 25th anniversary 9/11 observance ceremony, with the exception of any victim’s families, survivors or survivor’s families. In Pennsylvania, a ceremony is also planned at the Flight 93 national memorial , where United Airlines Flight 93 crashed after being hijacked. The morning observance will include a reading of the names of the passengers and crew members, followed by the ringing of the bells of remembrance. The afternoon ceremony is set to feature “remarks, keynote speakers, music and concludes with a public wreath-laying ceremony at the Wall of Names”, according to the National Park Service . On Saturday, another ceremony will take place at the Flight 93 national memorial, where 40 candle lanterns will be carried to the Wall of Names and placed beneath the names of each passenger and crew member. Additional ceremonies and memorial events are scheduled on Friday across the country as communities mark 25 years since the attacks. https://www.wirralglobe.co.uk/news/26496.text: Charity Pets Wirral New Brighton woman adopts puppy mill survivor Rosa By Jessica McKeown Reporter Share 0 Comments Rosa with her awards at Wirral Food and Drink Festival (Image: ROLDA) This article is brought to you by our exclusive subscriber partnership with our sister title USA Today, and has been written by our American colleagues. It does not necessarily reflect the view of The Herald. A PUPPY mill survivor has found a new lease of life and is now winning top prizes at dog shows. Rosa, a chihuahua rescued from neglect in Romania, was taken in by animal welfare charity ROLDA in October last year and later adopted by Annie Bond from New Brighton. Ms Bond spotted Rosa on Facebook just months after losing her 18-year-old chihuahua, Louie. Rosa wearing her ROLDA lead (Image: ROLDA) Ms Bond said: "The moment I saw her, I instantly knew I wanted to save her. "She looked so sad in the photograph. "I was terrified that she had never experienced what it was like to have a loving family. "Every time I looked at her, she broke my heart. "I was feeling incredibly lonely after losing Louie, and I didn’t want Rosa to feel that same sense of loneliness and sadness either. "I remember thinking that maybe she needed me just as much as I needed her." Annie with her previous dog Louie (Image: ROLDA) Rosa arrived in the UK in January after a 1,300-mile journey from Romania. The pair quickly formed a close bond, and Ms Bond said Rosa has helped her cope with the loss of Louie. She said: "These past few months with Rosa have genuinely been some of the happiest of my life. "I love her more than words can say, and we have formed the most incredible bond. "She isn’t just my dog, she’s my best friend, my little shadow and a huge part of my family. Rosa with her new best friend Saffie (Image: ROLDA) "I will never be able to thank ROLDA enough for rescuing Rosa and giving us the chance to find each other. "They didn’t just save a dog; they helped heal a broken heart. "Without ROLDA, I would never have met this amazing little girl who has changed my life in ways I never thought possible." Since settling into her new home, Rosa has even begun taking part in dog shows, winning Best Rescue Dog and Best in Show at the Wirral Food and Drink Festival in New Brighton. Rosa in her new jumper (Image: ROLDA) Ms Bond now hopes her story will encourage others to consider adopting rescue animals. She said: "I hope our story encourages others to support ROLDA or consider adopting a rescue dog. "You may think you’re rescuing them, but in so many ways, they rescue you too. "Rosa certainly rescued me, and I will be forever grateful." ROLDA is marking its 20th anniversary this year and continues to rescue, rehabilitate, and shelter animals in need. Photograph: Neil Hall/EPA Gas European gas prices soar to four-year high over winter supply fears Jump fuelled by fears of further Middle East supply disruptions amid reports of US-Israeli plans to strike Iran Lauren Almeida Mon 26 Oct 2026 06.35 EDT Last modified on Mon 26 Oct 2026 07.28 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google European gas prices have jumped to levels not seen since 2022 as fears continue to grow around the continent’s supply this winter and the conflict in the Middle East. Wholesale gas prices hit €97 (£81) a megawatt-hour on Monday, as temperatures across Europe fell and traders priced in stronger demand for heating. The UK’s month ahead contract also rose by 4% to 240p a therm, its highest level since December 2022 when prices were rocketing after Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine. The jump in gas prices comes as fears grow that there could be further supply disruptions in the Middle East, amid reports the US and Israel have drawn up plans for renewed strikes against Iran after the US midterm elections. Those reports helped send the oil price as high as $117 a barrel on Friday. The international Brent crude benchmark retreated about 2% on Monday but remains over $114 a barrel. Europe is also facing a shortage of stored gas reserves as it heads into winter with stores at their lowest level in more than a decade owing to a slowdown in exports from Qatar and an increase in consumption in the summer to power refrigeration and cooling. European storage is now about 75% full, against a seasonal average closer to 80%. Britain’s energy regulators have said the country is expected to pay some of the highest energy costs in Europe this winter amid a reliance on imports to ensure a steady supply. The UK has some of the smallest gas stores in Europe after decades of relying on homegrown production from the North Sea. The UK paid a record £4bn on power imports over the year ending in August, according to figures from the Office for National Statistics, of which half was spent on electricity imported from France. It has also made near-record payments over the past year to fire up gas plants while wind and solar farms have been paid to turn off because of bottlenecks in the grid. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Business Today Get set for the working day – we'll point you to all the business news and analysis you need every morning after newsletter promotion Meanwhile, British households face growing energy bills, which are predicted to rise 16% in January to reach the equivalent of about £2,000 for the typical annual dual fuel bill. European stock markets rose slightly on Monday on the weaker oil price, with the Stoxx Europe 600 – which tracks the biggest companies on the continent – up by 0.3% in early trading on Monday. The UK’s blue chip FTSE 100 rose by 0.4%.
